step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage fully differential op-amp with switched-capacitor CMFB
step1_figure.description: The circuit consists of a first-stage folded/telescopic diff-amp with SC CMFB (Fig. 26.54) biased by the circuit in Fig. 26.52, cascaded with a second-stage output buffer with SC CMFB (Fig. 26.56), operating under non-overlapping two-phase clocking.

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity-gain frequency (fun) of the two-stage operational amplifier determined by input transconductance and compensation capacitance

equation.explanation: The unity gain frequency is governed by the input differential pair transconductance gm and the Miller compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Diff-pair bias current ID = 20 uA, Vov = 100 mV, Cc = 50 fF

sky130_expected.calculation: gm = 2*ID/Vov = 2 * 20uA / 0.1V = 0.4 mS. With Cc = 50 fF: fun = 0.4e-3 / (2 * pi * 50e-15) = 1.27 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depending on tail current and exact parasitic capacitances in Sky130, fun will typically reside around 1.0 to 1.5 GHz.

settling_time.description: Time required for the differential and common-mode outputs to settle within target error band during phi2 phase

equation.explanation: Settling time during closed-loop/feedback evaluation phase phi2 must be under 3 ns for multi-hundred MHz operation as demonstrated in Fig. 26.60.
equation.assumptions: Non-overlapping clocks at 10 MHz to 100 MHz clock rate, load capacitance ~250 fF.

sky130_expected.calculation: For a single-pole closed-loop response with tau = 1/(2*pi*fun) ~ 125 ps, settling to within 1% requires approx 4.6*tau ~ 0.6 ns. With slew and non-dominant poles, settling is ~1.5 ns to 3 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Target settling time stated in text (p. 903) for optimized sizing is < 3 ns.

output_common_mode_voltage.description: Steady-state common-mode output level established by the output buffer SC CMFB loop

equation.explanation: The switched-capacitor CMFB forces the average of the differential outputs vop and vom to equal the ideal reference voltage VCM.
equation.assumptions: CMFB loop is stable and in negative feedback; VCM = 0.5 V as configured in the netlist.

sky130_expected.calculation: Ideal VCM is 0.50 V. With steady-state switching settling, Vocm settles to 0.50 V within switch charge-injection offset (< 20 mV).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The SC network transfers charge each clock cycle to lock the average output to VCM.

diff_amp_output_cm_voltage.description: DC common-mode voltage at the output of the first-stage diff-amp

equation.explanation: The first stage SC CMFB circuit forces the output common-mode level of the diff-amp to track Vbias1.
equation.assumptions: Vbias1 is generated by the bias circuit (Fig 26.52) referencing VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: Vbias1 in a 1.8V design is typically around 0.6 V to 1.1 V depending on PMOS diode drops (VDD - Vthp - Vovp).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Sets the operating point and gate bias for the second stage output buffer PMOS devices.

total_quiescent_power.description: Total DC power dissipation of the op-amp and bias generation circuitry

equation.explanation: Sum of currents through bias generator branches, diff-amp branches, and output buffer stages multiplied by supply rail VDD.
equation.assumptions: VDD = 1.8 V, nominal branch currents of 20 uA - 80 uA per leg.

sky130_expected.calculation: Total current for bias generator (approx 4 branches ~ 80 uA), diff-amp (40 uA), and output buffers (2 * 40 uA = 80 uA) gives I_total ~ 200 uA. P = 1.8 V * 200 uA = 360 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected quiescent current ranges between 100 uA and 400 uA under 1.8V VDD.

step3_testbench.description: Simulation testbench for two-stage op-amp with SC CMFB, driving non-overlapping clock generation at 100 MHz, running transient settling analysis for common-mode and differential voltages, and reporting DC operating point power.
